scope: BiDi local observer/diagnostic pump lifetime after successful local page or browser closure; no network-idle semantics expansion
source_state: Six uncommitted BiDi files; session.rs unchanged. Other agents own other checkout changes.

guarantees: Successful local page closure broadcasts a shared observer close signal to all aliases and finishes their idle/diagnostic pumps, even if the remote peer sends no contextDestroyed event.
Browser/connection shutdown finishes retained page diagnostic pumps without waiting for the broadcast channel sender to be dropped.
Diagnostic setup rejects known-closed resources before reusing cached readiness and checks closure again after acknowledged global setup.
Existing cancellation-safe setup workers and finite 5s setup budgets remain; all 111 BiDi tests include pre-ACK event delivery, cancellation/reuse, and silent-ACK timeout/retry coverage.
limitations: Lost or timed-out remote subscription acknowledgements with unknown remote subscription IDs cannot be reconciled/reclaimed by this change. Retrying can allocate another unknown remote subscription.
Weak session observer registry entries are pruned on subsequent lookup, not synchronously on every Drop; a dormant peak set of dead weak keys can remain until another lookup.
Caller-retained closed page handles still own local diagnostic history and finished task handle metadata; this evidence demonstrates worker/receiver lifetime, not zero retained heap bytes.
Closure racing immediately before close-receiver creation can still wait for the existing finite setup budget; post-ACK closure checks prevent late pump installation.
Controlled peers and unit tests do not establish Firefox heap plateau, remote subscription cleanup under lost replies, or SOTA.
